name: Offset-centre 2R pointer with a sliding twist sleeve at the cuff
verdict: dead, not worth a GPU sweep: the offset centre (the idea) is monotonically harmful (gap 88.6 at o 0 -> 152 at 5 mm -> 224 at 10 -> 250 at 20); at o 0 it is the cuff-sleeve-3r limit, and its bench best 71.15 is DEGENERATE (q 1: hub 2 327 mm, link 1 199 mm, bar cap 274 mm off the skin, only the cuff end in band); best non-degenerate 88.62 vs 68.93
limiter: (1) rod line O->C converges on O at ~15 deg to the arm: the rod clamp sinks ~0.27 mm per mm of slide travel into the deltoid (boss contact 11 poses at o 0, 139/220 at o 10); (2) the bar's run down the lateral arm (a quarter of all metal samples) is 0-4 % in band, median >= 32 mm, in every config: its roll is set by a1 x dh, not by the arm, so it must clear every axial rotation; (3) J2 hub 0-4 % in band (posterior-lateral cap filled by the elevated arm); red team: 11 across-body poses (plane >= 110) lose the cuff end inside the body, pinch 0.25 mm at the rod clamp (plane 122 elev 31 axial -80 flex 122)
note: bench fast Bench(60,160), K3 march, K2 dense (values + axes), part clearance >= 1 mm + 1 mm sampling slack, bar over link 1 by construction; spec fixed: C0 on the bench skin (q90 of the arm's own outer skin), U at real size (ring + cheeks); headline = bench best k 113 (degenerate, see verdict); best non-degenerate k 86: gap 88.62 reach 0.7625 follow 0.8833 ib14 0.4225 ib10 0.2431 contact 0.2045
